### Build 321 (b321b) - every face happy at a 100, one saucer

*"Ensure the characters expression change on the mood of the grade, the
alien still looks mad even after the hundred.. ensure all characters are
happy when they get the 100"* and *"in the background of the alien there
is a ufo, a second one comes in.. shouldn't that same one just move?"*

- **Measured, not looked at: 18 of the 30 were not happy at a 100** on
  6a387e2. Slanted eyes of light read as a scowl (the Masked One, Ronin,
  Umbra, Inferno, Astral, Zenith, Celestial, Orion's visor), the Alien
  kept its brow and its frown, the Sheriff squinted, the Detective
  stared. Only the faces already using `joy()` were happy.
- **The fix is one block at the end of `tools/reactions-table.py`**
  (`happy()`), applied to a 100 and a 90+: the open eyes go and the face's
  own happy pieces come in and stay - `joy()` (its closed eyes turned up)
  where they show on the face, or `glee()` (two arches of the eyes' own
  light, a soft wide one under a bright core) where the eyes are light in
  a dark face; `grin()` where a mouth is missing or flat. The moves before
  the pose are untouched. A prop with **front 2** is drawn ON THE FACE
  (inside the group holding the eyes), so the head's fit and every head
  move carry it - `reactCharacter()` handles it.
- **The Alien's brow is its own part now (`cx-brow`)** - so are Tempest's
  and Frost's brows and mouths. A 100 lifts the Alien's brow right off and
  turns the frown over; no grade wears the scowl (pass: level mouth; fail:
  let down). Its resting face is unchanged (asked for in build 271).
- **A fail is let down, never cross.** A face that rests in a smile turns
  it over (the Detective, the Hacker, Tempest, Frost); eyes that slant
  down to the nose drop and narrow to dim slits; Tempest's and Frost's
  brows go level. A pass keeps the face the character rests in.
- **The hundo effect's reaction covers the glee as well as the eyes**
  (`R.cover`), so it comes back with the pose when the effect ends.
- **One saucer.** On a 100 the reaction's saucer (`.cx-rx-ufo`) hovers over
  the head; the special then brought a second one (`.cx-sp-alufo`). Now,
  on a 100, the special's saucer is hidden and the reaction's one flies
  over the cow, beams it up and comes home (`cxsp-al-rxufo`, same clock as
  `cxsp-al-ufo`). Off the results screen (no saucer up) the special's own
  saucer swoops in as before. **The same mistake on the Detective**: his
  100 holds the reaction's magnifier and his special brought a second one
  out of the coat; on a 100 the special's glass starts and ends where the
  held one is and the two cross over in the special's fade. The other 28
  sceneries were audited: their props are weather, sparks, leaves or
  meteors (more of a kind, not a second copy of one thing).
- **Faceless drawings** (the Koi's bowl, Void's hood of flares) draw no eyes
  or mouth at all; the gate reports them by that, it does not pass them as
  happy.
- **Gate: `check_b321b_moods`** - the face's mood read off its shapes in the
  face's own units (a filled eye's or brow's droop towards the nose, a drawn
  eye's arch, the mouth's middle against its corners): every face happy at a
  100 and at 90+ (4s and 8s in), a fail never happy and no brow scowling,
  every face back on its happy 100 after the Confetti and UFO reactions and
  happy right through the special after them, one saucer and one magnifier
  at every moment (saucers counted by shape: a filled disc 4+ units across,
  3x as wide as tall), the saucer over the beam. Fails on 6a387e2.

### Build 321 (b321g) - Nova is an explorer, his crew are the characters, existing accounts meet him

Madison: *"he calls himself the app maker, don't do that. The cutscene where
it shows the planet and the planet explosion is ass ... Mention how during
the ship explosion a lot of characters or people on the ship went missing
too and you need to find them ... Mr nova screen when meeting a new player,
it's great. I almost feel like that should be the one shown to all the
existing profiles, but at the end it can go over the ones they have
unlocked ... still give the tool tips but after the main menu ones ...
ensure nova still says good bye and they'll talk again. AFTER the nova intro
that's when the what's new screen will show up."*

- **Nova never made the app.** He is "a space explorer and an instructor"
  (`novaIntroLines`, the 7.8 release note, What's New). Gate: no line of his,
  nor RELEASE_NOTES[0], matches made-the-app phrasing.
- **The lore: his crew went missing in the wreck, and the characters ARE
  them.** A character is *found*, like a badge and a secret flare. The
  introduction has a crew line with `novaCrewRow()` (characters you have,
  then cut-outs of missing ones, `charSilhouetteSVG`) and "N of M characters
  found" (`novaCrewTally` = Customize's character tally).
- **The wreck is redrawn (`buildNovaWreck`, `NW` timings in ms).** Home's
  own planet (`buildCosmicHero(false)` with `heroCrackStageFor = 0`, orbit
  badges hidden by `.nw2` CSS) in a square camera (`.nw2-cam`, container
  query units); Supernova's crack forms on it (`crackFormArm(hero, 0,
  CRACK_TOP)` at 0.9s, warmed while he says hello); it trembles, swells and
  goes at 3.5s: flash, fireball, a shockwave in the plane of the rings and a
  spherical one, 28 sparks, embers, dust that stays as a nebula; the planet
  breaks into 17 shards of ITSELF (`nwShards`: 7 wedges x crust/mantle + a
  3-piece core; every shared edge is one jagged polyline used both ways, so
  they fit at the blast) painted with `nwPlanetPaint` (the hero's sphere svg
  cropped and serialised to an image, under Supernova's burn), their broken
  edges glowing then cooling (`.nw2-hot`). His ship (`NW_SHIP_SVG`: hull,
  fins, nacelles, canopy, four lit portholes, his star, running lights,
  engine flames) is hit at 3.88s, its engines die, a breach burns, it
  tumbles away end over end trailing smoke, and six escape pods (his crew)
  fly out with beacons. Web Animations on transform/opacity only, no filter;
  the last keyframe is the resting style, which is all Reduce motion shows.
- **Existing accounts meet him once (`playNovaMeeting`).** Gated on the
  ACCOUNT: `store.novaMet` (`NOVA_MEET_REV` 1), default 0 in
  `applyLoadedData` (deliberately "not met", like tourRev), set at sign-up,
  merged by the higher in `mergeSameAccount` (a copy from an older build
  that drops it cannot bring him back). It plays from `maybeShowIntro` on
  the first Home where What's New is due (`INTRO_REV` 5, local): the
  introduction with `{ existing: true }` (greeted by username; Skip jumps to
  the recap, `skipTo`) ending in the recap - `novaRecapCard` (rank, level,
  badges, characters, secret flares found as Home's planet counts them) and
  his lines about it; then What's New CHAINED (`showIntroPopup({ chained,
  then })`: no second hello, ends "Show me"); then `startNovaReturnTour()` =
  `mainMenuTourSteps(true)` + `NOVA_NEW_TIPS_321` (the planet, the new
  Profile, the calendar's tab); then `novaGoodbye()` ("I'll speak with you
  again", id `nova-intro` so every hold that waits on him still does). No
  welcome bonus. `novaMeetOn` holds everything `whatsNewHolds` holds for the
  whole meeting, and `endNovaMeeting` gives the held pop-ups their turn. A
  device whose account already met him gets What's New alone ("Hello again").
  New accounts are unchanged: introduction, the seven main-menu tips
  (`mainMenuTourSteps(false)`), the bonus.
- **Gate `check_b321g_nova`** (fails on 6a387e2). Moved to this decision:
  `check_b320f_nova` (the story's words: explorer and crew, not "made this
  app"; What's New on its own needs `novaMet`), `check_b319_levelnote` (the
  note is said in the chained What's New too), check-tours (`novareturn`
  scenario; `startMainMenuTour` counts `mainMenuTourSteps`), check-chat's
  introduction (the meeting first, then What's New, tips and goodbye, once).
- **This release is VERSION 9** (*"This is gonna be version 9 ... show a
  version 8 with some of this stuff but put in parenthesis not launched"*).
  `RELEASE_NOTES[0]` is `version: "9"` (sound effects and Android vibration,
  both off by default; sign in first; rankings that match Profile; Nova; and
  one "Everything From Version 8" bullet). Build 320's "7.8" entry is
  `version: "8", notLaunched: true`, shown as "Version 8 (not launched)".
  Home's label, What's New's eyebrow and Nova's "what's new in version 9"
  all read `RELEASE_NOTES[0].version`. The newest entry is also Welcome's
  `showWhatsNew()`, so its items keep icons. Nova's What's New opens with a
  "Sound effects" row (WHATS_NEW_320 `sound`).
- **The version history lists every item as a bullet, in full**
  (`.releasehistory-list`: title, then what it does). It used to print a
  group's titles joined by commas, which is why it read thin. Builds before
  97 are not in this repo's git, so 2.0/3.0/Beta keep their existing text
  (now shown in full) rather than gaining anything that cannot be sourced.
  At the bottom, `#releasehistory-home`: a black "Back to Home" (`.next.ghost`,
  Quit test's look). check-fixes' Release History check moved: no back link
  at the top, Back to Home at the bottom.

### Build 321 (b321d) - the grain is the clean look, a dirtier dirtiest, a bevel, an engraved back, a simple badge in your hand

Madison: *"the semi dirty look adds a lot of texture to the badges and almost
makes them look better. Could be make that the normal tone ... and then just
redo the dirty scale so the dirtiest would be dirtier, a noticeable less shine
and less glow ... the backside stamp ... needs to look more engraved though and
legit ... especially where like the color meets the silver, ensure the sides
are good too ... THERE IS WAY TOO much going on here."*

- **`BADGE_DIRT` is a table BY STAGE now** (arrays indexed 0-4), not a
  per-unit-of-stage scale. Stage 0 - every new badge, every clean one - wears
  what build 320's stage 1-2 looked like: a fine grain in the metal and the
  enamel (`grain`, `grainE`), a faint patina in soft patches (`film`), grime
  at the foot of every wall (`grime`), and still most of its shine. Stage 4
  is far past build 320's dirtiest: highlights nearly gone (`gloss` .92),
  flat warm metal, a heavy film and soft dust flecks (`dust`). `glow` and
  `shine` are the badge-in-your-hand's glow and face light per stage. Hue
  never changes (the ±12 degree gate still holds). A grey token wears none.
- **One noise table (`badgeNoiseTable`, `badgeNoiseAt`)**, 128 texels,
  tileable, read bilinearly; `badgeSmudge` reads it too. **All wear noise is
  read once per OUTPUT pixel per row** (`wearRow`), never per sample: per
  sample it doubled a case-sized render for nothing. The fine grain fades out
  below ~1.6 output px per token unit (`gF`) so the 4x-reference sampling
  gate (check_b318) still holds. Dust is two readings at odd angles: a
  thresholded single reading printed square flecks on the table's lattice.
- **THE COLOUR MEETS THE SILVER AT A BEVEL** (`bvTop`, `bvFoot`, `bvR`,
  `bvCrown`, `bevelMax`; the inner profile `BADGE_PROF_IN` over distance
  from the colour in token units). Build 319's soft wall (`wallMax`, still
  in the table, no longer used by the inner side) took out the hairline and
  with it the step. A ~35 degree bevel, ~1.9 units wide, rounded at both
  ends by smooth min/max: in shadow on a plate's top and left edges, a
  bright line on its bottom and right. **check_b319_badges' seam metric is
  moved**: only scans against the light must have no dark hairline; the
  shadowed side is check_b321d's bevel check.
- **THE BACK IS RENDERED LIKE THE FRONT (`renderBadgeBack`)**: the same
  geometry, mirrored (fields read at the mirrored column, x-slopes negated -
  the light stays top-left), the same rim, outer wall and bevel down into a
  recessed BRUSHED field, and the name ENGRAVED as a height field
  (`badgeBackLayout` draws the words; `BADGE_BACK_RELIEF`): walls lit by
  their normals, a cast shadow along the side the light comes from, a matte
  darker floor, grime in the cuts. It wears the badge's stage.
  `badgeBackEntry(unit, W, stage, draft)` caches by size and stage;
  `badgeBackFaceFlatURL` is build 320's flat drawing, used only if the render
  throws. **Not rendered in the tap**: the inspect view puts up a cached back
  if there is one, the draft 140ms after the lift starts (the front's draft is
  at 60ms), and the finish (and a new stage's back after a rub) in its idle
  work. Cost ~ the coin's front face.
- **The coin's side is rounded over** (`badgeEdgeURL(unit, tone, stage)`):
  slices near a face are dark (the tone the face's outer wall ends on), the
  middle ones lighter, and the whole edge dims and warms with the stage. With
  no tone it is build 320's edge exactly - the cutscene's coin (builder C's)
  calls it that way.
  (superseded in 326: the side is lit by which way each stretch faces, and
  the cutscene's coin uses the toned slices too - b326b.)
- **Seated** (token side only; the slot's lip, wall and floor are untouched):
  a tight two-step contact shadow round the token (`.badge-contact`), and a
  first, crisp seat-shade step (`BADGE_SEAT_SHADE[0]`, .22 units at .5) - the
  hole's lip lying over the token's top-left edge. check_b242's
  `rgba(0,0,0,.42)` shadow is unchanged.
- **The badge in your hand says almost nothing**: its name, "Rub to clean
  it." only while dirty (nothing - not "clean" - once clean, even right after
  a rub), a quiet "Swipe to spin it.", Close. No kicker, Mastered,
  requirement, bar, count or care line. A badge not found: its name and one
  line, "12 of 35 hundos". **Moved**: check_b320g_inspect's words and hint
  checks, check_b319_badges' "Mastered on the card", check_b281's green bar.
- **Gate: `check_b321d_badges`** (fails on 6a387e2): stage-0 enamel grain,
  stage 4's highlights gone and p97 down a median 85+, the bevel's shadow and
  highlight on every badge, the back's engraving contrast and its wear, the
  simple words on both reference devices, and the stage-4 glow and face light
  at most .2.

### Build 322 (b322s) - sound and vibration, phase 1: the engine, the library, Settings

Madison: *"a setting in settings that will be off by default ... sound
effects ... I NEED you to ensure all the sounds and sound effects are unique
and make sense. Not sound effects you just find ... the main menu has a cool
dark kinda offset noise ... each hundo effect to have its own noise ... IF
there is any way to put Haptic Touch or a vibration for things that would be
awesome too."* All of it sits in one block after `saveTheme()`.

- **Every sound is synthesised in code; there are no audio files.**
  `SOUND_CATALOGUE` maps an id to `{ group, bus, cd, poly, hap, vol, desc,
  fn, demo }`; `fn(K, opts)` draws with the kit from `sndKit()`: `tone`
  (glides, paths, vibrato, filters), `fm` / `bell`, `noise` (white / pink /
  brown, swept filters, flutter), `click`, `thump`, `pluck` (Karplus-Strong,
  `sndKS`), `vox` (two vowel formants - the characters' and Nova's voices),
  `sparkle`, `arp`, and the generated reverb (`sndImpulse`) and delay sends.
  The identity: D as home, open fifths and ninths for anything good, a
  semitone or a fall for anything that is not, glassy FM for light, filtered
  air for movement, felt and metal for the badge case. 123 ids plus the Home
  ambience (`SOUND_AMBIENCE`). Cutscene and hundo scores read the app's own
  constants where they exist (`CASE_OPEN`, `HFX_UW`, `BADGE_CUTSCENE_MS`,
  `RU_HAND_MS`, `RANK_ATTN_MS`, `RANK_CUTSPIN_*`, `RANK_WINDUP_*`); the
  Fireworks shots, the UFO's beats and the Bubbles flourish (3.5s) are inline
  in their `hfx*` builders, so their times are copied into the score -
  **move one of those and move the score with it.**
- **Off, and free while off.** `theme.soundOn`, `theme.soundVolume` (0-1,
  default .7) and `theme.vibrate`, by the behaviour-toggle rule (the theme
  object, a `typeof` line in `loadTheme()`, `saveTheme()`). While sound is
  off no `AudioContext` is constructed at all; one is made on the first
  gesture after it is turned on (the Settings switch is one). The live graph
  is master (the volume, `.95 v^2`) -> a gentle limiter, with buses `ui`
  (1.6), `music` (.6, the ambience) and `cut` (1, cutscenes and hundo
  effects); a `cut` sound ducks the ambience. Per-id cooldown and polyphony,
  `SOUND_MAX_VOICES` (24) overall. Hidden page: the context is suspended;
  back: resumed, and the ambience only if its owner element is still in the
  document. `NovaSound.sync()` follows a setting that changed (the switch, the
  slider, a theme arriving from another device - `loadTheme()` calls it).
- **iPhone: the silent switch mutes it, on purpose.** `navigator.audioSession
  .type = "ambient"` where it exists, so somebody's own music keeps playing and
  Silent mode silences the app - the Settings hint says so.
- **Vibration is Android only, and iOS is still not possible.** WebKit has no
  `navigator.vibrate`; the `<input switch>` trick was tried on a device and
  fails (Known quirks) and is not retried. The switch shows only where
  `navigator.vibrate` exists on an Android user agent (desktop Chrome has the
  function and no motor). Each id's `hap` names a pattern in `SOUND_HAPTIC`;
  `playSound()` buzzes when vibration is on even with sound off.
- **The ambience (`amb.home`) is seamless by construction**: a 20s loop whose
  every frequency and LFO is a whole number of cycles per loop, loop-length
  noise, every event scheduled in the loops either side, rendered from 4s in
  (steady state) at `AMB_SR` 22050 with a cheap feedback-delay room (the
  convolver over 25s cost seconds of render), and a 0.5s seam crossfade.
- **API**: `playSound(id, opts)` (returns `{ length, stop }` or null),
  `startAmbience(id, { owner })`, `stopAmbience()`. All no-ops while off.
  **Phase 1 wires only Settings and the test page**; phase 2 wires the app.
- **Settings**: "Sound & vibration" between "Display & motion" and "Studying &
  tests" (`buildSoundSettings()`): Sound effects, the volume (shown only while
  on, saved on release), Vibration (Android). The Settings tour is unchanged
  (its copy is Nova's) - a step for this group is for whoever owns his lines.
- **`showSoundTest()`** - every id with a play button, by group, the ambience,
  and Play all. From the console, or a 0.75s press on Settings' build line
  (`.settings-buildline`, delegated in `NovaSound`). It is in `SCREENS`.
- **A GainNode is 1 until its first automation event** (`K.env` sets `.value
  = 0` first). Without it every sound starting part-way through a render
  quantum let one full-scale sample through - a click on the front of every
  sound, measured at 0.92 on one that should have peaked at .06.
- **Gate: `tools/check-sound.py`** (fails on 6a387e2): off by default (new,
  existing, non-boolean); no AudioContext after boot, taps and direct calls;
  the Settings group, the volume, Android-only Vibration, one running context
  on the switch, persistence across a reload, a gesture to wake it; cooldown,
  voice cap, hidden/visible, the ambience stopping with its screen; vibration
  without sound; every id renders offline (no limiter, volume 1) with a peak
  between .04 and .97 and a loudest-50ms RMS of .01+; **no two ids above .90
  similarity** (spectro-temporal shape, mean spectrum, envelope, length;
  pitch-tolerant to ~6 semitones), the metric proven able to fail (a sound
  against itself with another seed = 1.00; the timer's tick against its tock
  > .90); the ambience's seam step no bigger than the loop's 99.9th
  percentile step and its level within 1.5dB either side. Closest pair at
  this build: .85 (the Bronze and Sapphire flares).

### Build 322 (b322k) - sign in first, no second account by accident, the board says what Profile says

*"We need to really crack down on the leaderboard accuracy and crack down
on people's progress randomly going away or people somehow using two
accounts ... could we make it where it asks you to sign in first and then
you have to hit I'm new here sign up or something?"*

- **Welcome leads with Sign in** (`.welcome-signin`, the playbtn); **I'm
  new here** (`.welcome-new`, the ghost) opens `showSignUpCheck()` - "NEW
  TO NOVA?", what starting again costs, **Sign in instead** in the content
  group and **I'm new, continue** on the shared Continue floor - and only
  then What's New and the rest of sign-up. What's New's Back returns to the
  check. `shoot-flow.py` walks it (shot 2.8 `new-to-nova`); the sweep and
  check-positions mount it.
- **A device that still holds an account is offered it first.**
  `findAccountTrace()` = the code in localStorage, else the IndexedDB
  mirror's code, else a mirrored onboarded store. With one, Welcome reads
  "Welcome back", **Continue as <name>** ("Continue to your account" when
  only the code is known) and **Use a different account**
  (`welcomeTraceSkip`, this launch only). `continueWithTrace()` merges the
  same account back (`pullFromCloud`, never adopt) and lands on Home; a
  sign-up that stopped before Home is finished (`pendingMainMenuTour`); a
  dead code (`not-found`) is handed back like the launch link's.
- **`finishWelcomeStartFresh()` refuses to mint over a trace** unless the
  check screen showed that trace and the person tapped I'm new, continue on
  it (`signupTraceAck`). Then the old account's local copy is WIPED before
  the new code is minted - otherwise the "new" account is the old progress
  under a second code. `wipeLocalProgressAndSettings()` sets
  `accountWipedAt`, so a reset in this session is never offered back while
  its mirror deletes are still landing.
- **The username screen asks once about a name already on the board**
  (`nameTakenOnBoard`: case and spaces ignored, read from the
  `leaderboardRows` the app already fetches - `fetchBoardForInvites`, its
  15-minute throttle - never a progress read). "Someone named X already has
  an account. If that's you, sign in with your code." with **Sign in**; the
  floor button becomes **It's not me, continue**. Only the name is said.
- **Three account holes, each with a failing check on 6a387e2:**
  - *A non-adopt pull only ever merges the SAME account.* The mirror's
    code-only recovery pulled before the device held a code; if a sign-in
    or sign-up landed while the read was out, it merged one person's
    progress into the other's and then switched the code. `pullFromCloud`
    now answers `changed` when `syncCode` moved to a different code.
  - *A code whose store is gone lands on Home when its account comes down*
    (boot's launch pull, and the mirror-store recovery's pull). It used to
    leave Welcome up over the restored account, where Create an account
    pushed that same progress up under a second code.
  - *Linking retires the row the device was publishing under.* Sign-in and
    Link this device ADOPT first, which replaces `store.publicId`, then call
    `setSyncCode()` - which retired the adopted account's row (it came back
    on the next push) and stranded the abandoned one on the board for good.
    `pullFromCloud` records `adoptedOverPublic`; `setSyncCode` retires that.
- **The board's numbers are Profile's.** `boardNumbersOf(st)` builds every
  number a row carries (level, badges, hundos, xp, correct, tests, week,
  weekPoints, mystery, `rankFloor`) and is used by `buildLeaderboardRow()`
  AND `liveEntries()` - which carried its own half-copy, so your own card on
  the board showed the XP and right answers you last PUBLISHED. **The row
  now carries `rankFloor`** (lazy field), and `rankOfEntry(e)` /
  `rankWithFloor()` / `overallProgressOf(level, badges, rankFloor)` ask a
  row's rank exactly as `rankOf()` asks your own: someone held at a rank by
  build 314's floor was a rank lower on the board, the person card and the
  Friends list than on their Profile. Rows from older builds have no floor
  and read as before. The Virtual Room participant entries do not carry it
  (out of scope; they still use `rankOfStats`).
- **A row never goes backwards.** `writeLeaderboardRow()` is a transaction
  (read-then-write for the gates' stand-ins, a plain set for ones that
  cannot read): if the row on the server holds more `xp`, `correct` or
  `hundos` (`ROW_GROWS` - the numbers that only grow for an account; a
  reset is a new public id) nothing is written, the device drops its
  confirmation and reads the account again (`ensureCloudConfirmed`), and
  the row goes from the merge. Once only (`rowRecheckFor`): a row AHEAD of
  its own account (an old build wrote it) is corrected to the account. Cost:
  one read per row write. A row write that fails is retried on the next
  push rather than queued offline (it used to be a queued `set()` that could
  land a day late).
- **Gates:** `check-sync` 9a-9f (sign in first; the check; the name;
  device traces x4; board = Profile; no regressed row). All 20 fail on
  6a387e2.

### Build 322 (b322s) - sound, phase 2: wired into the app (all but four areas)

- **Generic taps are one delegated layer** (`sndForTap`, `SND_NO_GENERIC`,
  after the `playSound` wrappers): a primary button (`.next:not(.ghost)`,
  `.playbtn`) thocks - or is a step forward (`ob.step`) before onboarding is
  complete - any other button ticks, `.bottomtab` slides, `.navsegment
  .iconbtn` / `[role=tab]` flicks, `.back-link` steps back, a Tug/Battle
  `.choice` is `test.select`, Customize picks say what they picked
  (`.avatarchar-option` / `.swatch` / `.banner-opt` / `.hfx-opt`, or
  `ui.locked` on `.locked`), a checkbox toggles, a text field focuses. A
  specific sound made by the same tap wins: `opts.generic` gives way to any
  non-generic play in the last 220ms. A new screen needs nothing to get its
  taps; a new SPECIFIC sound just calls `playSound()` in its handler.
- **Not wired yet, on purpose** (being rebuilt in build 322): the results
  screen (grade, XP count/bar, "Found & unlocked"), the badge case cutscene
  and the Badges-tab case, the rank-up journey (cutscene, road map, card,
  Profile return) and the Profile card. `SND_NO_GENERIC` keeps generic taps
  off them too; take each selector out when its area is wired.
- **Specific hooks** - every one a single `playSound()` line, a no-op with
  sound and vibration off, never awaited by an animation: the test
  (`choose`, `runStreakLive` now RETURNS the tier it hit, `advance`, the star
  in `buildQuestionFlag`, `pauseRun` / `resumeRun`, `updateTimerDisplay`'s
  last ten seconds, `onTimeUp`, `saveAndExitTest`, `showCountdown`'s LOADING
  TEST); Home (planet, rank bubbles by tier, `homeLockedNudge`,
  `secretFlareTold`, `homeRingStreak` - a tap full, the pulse's streak at
  .45 gain - the daily ring's fill and its announce, `startAmbience` on the
  Home panel); notices (`showNoticeBar`, `showDailyAlert` unless live,
  `buildAppBanner` - invites are `chat.invite`); sheets (`mountSheetOverlay`
  opens with `overlay.dataset.sndOpen` or `ui.sheet.open` and closes on
  removal; the chat dock and the room chat sheet); chat (send, sendKind,
  reactions, `chat.receive` for somebody else's newer message after the
  first render, unless muted); Leaderboard (`selectBoard`, Find me, last
  week's congratulations = `lb.winner`); Virtual Room (lobby mount, ready,
  join via the roster's keys, `announceVroomLeave`, the countdown's 3-2-1 and
  go, the rope moving, another racer moving up, both end cutscenes); Nova
  (`novaType` blips, `novaTalk`'s arrival or What's New, the wreck's
  `cs.planet` on `NW`, every tooltip step); hundo effects (`playHundoFx` and
  `hfxCharReact`, stopped with the effect); badge inspect (lift, spin by
  speed, rub by dirt, a squeak per stage off, the sparkle when clean).
- **`let` inside a screen function that a hoisted inner function reads**:
  `drawLobbyRoster` runs before the line it sits on, so its `sndLobbyKeys`
  lives at the top of `showVirtualRoomLobby` - declared beside it, the TDZ
  error (swallowed by a try) emptied the lobby's first frame.
- **Gate**: `check-sound.py` section 9 drives the app with sound on and a
  spy on `NovaSound.play`: ambience, planet, tab bar, a Settings switch,
  LOADING TEST, wrong, right, star, pause/resume, next, Nova's blips, and last
  week's fanfare replacing the plain sheet sound.

- **Centred on its shape, out of the case too** (after b321c's
  `badgeSlotShift`). The badge in your hand (`.binspect-coin`) and the
  cutscene's coin (`.bc-coin`) carry `--sdx`/`--sdy` and move back by that
  share of their size with the independent `translate` property (so it
  composes with `bc-pop`'s transform), and `.binspect-spin`, `.bc-spin` and
  `.bc-sway` turn about the shape's own middle, so a turn never swings an
  off-centre shape (the C-ring) aside. The engraved back's words are centred
  on the visible shape too. The lift out of a slot, the drop back in and the
  cutscene's flight into its slot aim at the shape's middle in the slot
  (`slot centre - shift x size`), where the slot's own drawing is moved. The
  cutscene's coin takes its back warmed in idle (`warmBadgeCoinFaces`,
  `badgeCoinBackPx`) or the quick draft - never the finish as the scene
  builds. Gate: check_b321d_badges, all sixteen within 1px front and back
  (b316-work 8c729e8: the C-ring 34px off at the hand's size).

### Build 322 (b322s) - sound, phase 3: the badge case, the rank-up journey, the Profile card

- **The badge case.** The Badges tab's lid (`openBadgeCaseLid`) plays
  `badge.case.open` on CASE_OPEN from when the lid moves. The BADGE FOUND
  cutscene (`playBadgeCaseScene`) is scored on BC_T, beat by beat inside its
  own `at()` timers (so a skip silences what has not started): `cs.badge` at
  the coin (spin-up, the reveal chord at BC_T.intro, the glint at
  BC_T.glint); `bc.rise` with the lift; `badge.case.open` at latchL with
  `{ latch2, crack, swing, swingMs: 2.2 (the .bc-lid transition), light }`;
  `badge.spin` for each further badge; `badge.slide` over the front wall for
  BC_T.flyMs and `badge.drop` (with `ring`) as it seats. Every case open now
  carries the handle's little swing as the latches let go. **If BC_T or the
  lid's 2.2s change, the score moves with them** (the 2.2 is copied).
- **The rank-up journey**: `rank.road.scroll` on each camera glide
  (`rankUpRide`, `rankUpUpNext`), `rank.road.fill` for exactly the ride's
  `ms`, `rank.unlock.pop` as a circle opens (`rankUpArrive`),
  `rank.flare.zoom` at the hand-out, then the cutscene: `rank.attn`,
  `rank.whirl` on ACC/DEC at ignite, `rank.bang`, one `rank.windup` per
  breath on the planet-pulse ring's own peak (`windUp`'s beats) and
  `rank.swell` over the last `1 - RANK_WINDUP_FILL`, `rank.flash` (or
  `rank.sn.swell` + `rank.supernova`), `rank.crack` with `crackForm.play`,
  `rank.title` with `supernova-settle`. Then `rank.upnext` as Up next lifts,
  `rank.card` - a FADE now (b321e), redesigned to match - `rank.word` as the
  rank's name pops on Profile, `rank.xp.climb` with a ping at the exact
  moment each level lands on the sine-eased climb (`opts.marks`), and
  `rank.challenge.tick` when the level row ticks Met.
- **The Profile card** needs nothing of its own: its taps are the generic
  layer's, and its moments (the rank word, the climb, the tick) are the
  journey's.
- `SND_NO_GENERIC` now keeps only the journey's input blocker (a tap there
  reaches nothing, so it says nothing) and the surfaces with their own
  sounds.

### Build 323 (b323t) - the tab bar: a lens that pops out and follows, white labels, Calendar on the bar

*"When I change tabs by tapping or swiping over the Liquid Glass bottom tab
bubble doesn't pop out and follow. The Liquid Glass in the screenshot I
circled is good, that's the best, it should look more like that when that's
the tab you are on."* / *"the bottom tab icons and wording is that nice white
too and not the grey we have"*. Gated in `check_b323t_tabbar` (fails on
22bf429).

- **The bar is Home, Profile, Leaderboard, Calendar.** `#bottomtab-settings`
  is gone (Settings lives in Profile); `#bottomtab-calendar` (`data-dest`
  `calendar`) calls `showCalendarTab()` where it exists, `showCalendar()`
  otherwise. `syncActive()` lights Calendar for any `#stage .screen-calendar`
  that is SHOWING (not inside a `[hidden]` panel) - so it is right whether
  the calendar is its own screen or a pane - and Settings / the bug report
  light Profile. Every button lookup there tolerates a missing button. The
  stage observer watches `hidden` as well as `class` for that reason.
- **The resting pill is clear glass** (`.bottomtabs-slider::before`): no flat
  white wash (that was the "greyed out" look), a 34% hairline rim, a 50%
  specular along the top, a cool fringe along its top edge and a warm one
  along its bottom, a faint dark band inside the rim, a soft shadow. Same
  `inset:5px 2px`.
- **The lens** (`#bottomtabs-lens` > `.tab-lens-body`) lives on `<body>`, not
  in the bar: `[data-layout="modern"] .bottomtabs` is `overflow:hidden` (its
  sheen layer is 4x its width), which would clip the lens to the bar. It is
  measured once per touch (`lensMeasure`), `pointer-events:none`, z 201. On
  press it starts exactly the resting pill's size over the current tab and
  pops (taller than the bar by 18px, the tab's width plus 12px each side) on
  its way to the pressed tab; on a drag it follows the finger (a
  `translate3d` on the box, its width a `scaleX` blended between the tabs it
  is between); on release it glides to the tab and shrinks back into the
  pill there, which fades back in under it (`.bottomtabs.lens-up` hides the
  pill while the lens is out - one piece of glass, never two). The tabs
  under it are magnified by an inline `transform` (up to 1.14).
- **The pop and the shrink are Web Animations, not transitions.** A tap's
  press and release land in the same frame, and a transition retargeted with
  a delay HOLDS wherever the first one had got to: the lens froze a few
  pixels into its pop. The shrink is queued behind the pop (its own delay, no

### Build 324 (b324v2) - Nova in a Virtual Room, and the Sheriff for beating him

Madison: *"If you want to, you can now invite him to virtual rooms, but he
will be super hard to beat ... he would need to answer questions right within
like 4 seconds and almost every time make a 95-100 ... That's gonna be the
sheriff's new challenge now, is beating nova in a virtual rooms match. Can be
any of them ... He's invitable like anyone else now and can join. When he
joins make him delay the ready up."*

- **He is a participant, key `nova`, written by ONE device.** The host's
  invite sheet has his row first (`buildNovaInviteRow`); Invite writes
  `participants.nova` (`novaVrEntry`: avatarChar `nova`, level 80, every
  badge, `titan_rank` banner, `by` = the inviting device) through the same
  field paths a player's client uses, so every device - older builds too -
  draws and counts him as a player. A fixed key means at most one Nova.
  `buildAvatarCharSVG("nova")` returns his head (framed like the others,
  shoulders faded); he is in no picker. His row reads "Supernova" (no
  level) and opens his own card (`vroomPersonEntry`).
- **The driver** (`novaVrDrive`) is the inviter's own listener plus a 200ms
  clock; it stops itself on any device that is not `by`. Lobby: not ready
  while the room cannot start; once it can, `prep` ("Readying..." on his
  row, on every device) for 3.2-6.5s, then ready. A match: spends his
  ready and last race's fields, then plays the mode by its rules -
  Race (progress per answer, finish with `computeRunXp` on his answers,
  `revealDone`), Tug (read-in, pull for clock left, the pauses), Battle
  (hits 5/7, seeded powers used ~1s after, a freeze or flip on him slows
  him). His presence rides the inviter's beat (`novaVrPresencePatch`).
- **Difficulty** (`novaVrPlan`, seeded by room code + startAt): 85% of
  matches he misses 0.3-2.8% of questions, 15% ("off day") 3.5-7.5%; ~97.9%
  right overall, 90% of 30/50-question runs at 95%+. Every answer 2-4s
  (mean of three draws, ~3s). Measured by simulating each mode's rules: a
  Race is won by missing FEWER than him (equal misses, his speed wins);
  Tug and Battle are throughput - ~3s answers AND fewer misses.
  `novaVrTimeScale` is a gate hook only.
- **The host leaving takes him along** (`novaVrLeavePatch`, one write,
  "X and Nova left"); a host whose phone died goes stale with him, and
  the next host removes him (`novaVrOrphanCheck`). `vroomHostKeyOf` never
  picks him.
- **Beating him** (`novaVrOutcome`): Race - more of the room's XP, or the
  same XP faster (exactly level is a draw); Tug/Battle - your side won and
  he was on the other. Draw, same side, or his forfeit (not finished / not
  present) is not a win. `novaVrAfterMatch` runs once per match from the
  race standings, `showTugResult` and `showBattleResult`: `store.novaBeaten`
  (default false, OR-merged), the Sheriff's unlock card
  (`playUnlockSpotlight`, above the race standings: `.rs-spot` z 440 there),
  then one DM (`novaSendDM`, id `vr:<code>@<startAt>`).
- **The Sheriff's feat is `novabeat`** ("Beat Nova in a Virtual Room match
  (any mode)"), card "Not yet"/"Done" (`UNLOCK_WINDOWS`, `w.status`).
  `weektop3x3` stays defined, unread; `settleWeeklyWin` no longer queues
  him. `migrateSheriff324()` (in `applyLoadedData`, once per account via
  `sheriffMoved324`) puts him in `legacyChars` for anybody with 3+ podiums.
- XP, hundos, matches and wins are what the same match against a person
  pays; he has no board row and is not in `friendPublicIds()`.
- Gate `check_b324v2_novavr` (fails on c6a50b9). Moved: check_b232's
  "a third week on the podium hands over Poseidon" (now: counted, hands
  over nothing); check_b323v's invite test reads a friend's button, not
  the first (Nova's).

### Build 324 (b324v3) - Nova a little slower in Tug of War and Battle

Madison, asked whether to slow him in those two modes: *"Yes"*. Both
modes reward getting through questions quickly, so at 2-4s an answer a

is added to every answer in Tug and Battle only (`novaVrMs`; 2.75-4.75s,
~3.75s on average). A Race is untouched. Simulated with each mode's rules

1-11 -> 22-26; 98% at 3s 51-55 -> 84-96. Gate `check_b324v3_tug` (fails on

### Build 325 (b325a) - the way on rises, Confetti dims, a glow that is its own colour, the chat stays, every card's edge, the water, no tick, every character centred

Madison, Oct 18: *"The continue to review button, re run button, and main
menu button just show up really fast. Have them slide up from the bottom
like how the next question button does"*; *"the new hundo effects the
screen goes slightly dim ... ensure the default one is the same"*; *"the
number 100 lights up on a delay and it's not a smooth transition at the
end"*; *"The chat button disappears and comes back during hundo effect?
... it can stay"*; *"the edges of it have that nice hard glow, ensure all
the other boxes on the result screen match this"*; *"he holds his breath
even before the water and holds it after it's gone ... The fish coming by
and the random shadow black thing is bad"*; *"What's up with the check
mark for the 70 %? Don't do that"*; *"almost every character and its stuff
is not centered, they are all near the top"*.

- **THE WAY ON RISES (`rsRise`, next to `rsLand`).** The container is
  simply there; each button runs `rs-rise` - the Next question pill's own
  move (`qnext-rise`: up from its own height and 3rem below where it rests,
  in by 35%, .62s on `cubic-bezier(.16,.84,.3,1)`) - a row at a time
  (`RS_RISE_ROW_MS` 90). `.rs-rising` comes off when the last one is up,
  so `.next:active` is the button's own again. Everywhere a run ends: the
  results (the reveal's last step, so it still waits for every card, the
  XP fill and a hundo's tail; the camera follows to where they REST,
  `rsFollow`), the review and back to the results (160ms after the
  screen, no scroll), the race board's exits (`.vrc.is-done`), Tug of War
  and Battle's end screens, the room results (after its level bar,
  `vroomResultsAt`). **The daily question's Exit rises too**, the pill's
  own `is-rising` with its delay set to 1.9s - after the verdict's XP line
  (.9s) and last line (1.45s + .45s) - into the exact spot Submit answer
  had (build 317's "the button does not move" still holds: it is where it
  RESTS). Reduce motion: nothing moves. `check_b317_daily` now waits for
  the rise before reading Exit's spot.
- **CONFETTI DIMS (`celebrate(.., { dim })`, `.stardust-dim`).** The
  Fireworks' own dim - the same night-blue fall-off at .5 - in over .42s
  (Fireworks' 6% of 7s), held to 1.5s, out by 2.9s with the last motes;
  the box is lifted over it (`hfx-over`, 3s) as the Fireworks lift theirs.
  Only `playHundoFx` asks for it; a Virtual Room win's burst is plain.
  **Confetti has a tail now (`HUNDO_FX_TAIL_AT.confetti` 3050)**: without
  an entry the results fell back to 1.5s and the buttons rose under the
  dim at .5; now they (and the first unlock) wait until it is at 0.
  **Bubbles has no dim at all**, measured - flagged, not changed.
  (superseded in 326: every effect shares one dim, `hfxDim`;
  `.stardust-dim` and `celebrate()`'s `{ dim }` are deleted - b326a.)
- **THE 100's GLOW WAS NEAR-BLACK FOR .9s, THEN SNAPPED.** The landing
  transitions the number's `filter` over `RS_HUNDO_CROSS_MS`; its
  drop-shadow colour was `color-mix(in srgb, var(--hfx-b) 40%,
  transparent)`, and Chromium interpolates that as `rgba(1,0,0,.4)` frame
  after frame until the end value lands - so the number lit "on a delay"
  and jumped on the last frame. Read off `getComputedStyle` each frame;
  nothing in the code says so. `hfxTintVars` now writes the glow as a
  plain `rgba()` (`--hfx-glow`). **Never transition anything whose colour
  is a color-mix(); write the colour out.** The cards' new edges use r,g,b
  triplets for the same reason.
- **A HUNDO EFFECT HOLDS FOCUS SOFTLY (`cutscene-soft`, `syncCutsceneSoft`,
  `CUTSCENE_SOFT_SEL`).** A full-page effect still holds toasts, invites
  and the chat dot (b320c), but while it is the only scene up the chat
  button stays put, visible and tappable, and an open chat stays open;
  when it ends there is nothing to slide back (`cutsceneEndedSoft`). A
  real scene over its tail (the badge case) takes the class off and the
  button leaves as before.
- **EVERY CARD'S EDGE IS THE HUNDO BOX'S (`--rs-edge`).** The hundo box is
  a rim in its colour at full strength, an inset 1px line at 55% and an
  inset 30px glow at 26%. The XP card (blue), Found & unlocked (violet),
  a pass (green), a fail (red), a retake (amber/green), the default 100
  (gold), the room's waiting card and the badge box carry the same three
  in their own colour; washes unchanged. A grade short of 100 eases into
  its edge as it lands (.6s); a 100's rim lands with its effect, untouched
  (the UFO's stays unlit until its beam). The default's gold rim is now at
  full strength, so `check_b317_hundobox`'s and `check_b313_fx`'s
  `GOLD_BORDER` is `rgb(242, 211, 138)` (was `rgba(.., .2)`).
- **UNDERWATER: DRAWN FISH, NO MANTA (`hfxFishURL`).** The manta sprite
  (the "shadow black thing") is deleted. Three species, each lit from
  above with fins, markings and a catch-lit eye: a silver school (an
  iridescent stripe), a clownfish (three black-edged white bands clipped
  to the body), a blue tang (its sweep and a yellow tail). The school

- **THE BREATH IS HELD AGAINST THE FACE.** `hfxUwScreen` compared the

- **THE WATER'S CLOCK IS THE DRAIN ANIMATION'S OWN TIME.** `hfxSea`'s

- **NO TICK ON A PASS (`reactCharacter`).** The front sign layer has no

- **EVERY CHARACTER CENTRED IN ITS CIRCLE (`centreFigure`,

### Build 325 (b325b) - names that fit the back of every badge, one nameplate, latches that hook, one corner

Madison: *"the title of the back of them though aren't visible though,
especially for some depending on the shape. This needs to be fixed badly"*;
*"the thing on the top that says 'Nova - Class 26E' does not look 3d. It
looks like a sticker. The thing on the front that says level one badge case
is the same way, and that one has a weird placement because it's sitting on
top of stuff. Would it make more sense if that one was just combined with
the other one and put on top?"*; *"some of the metal things on the corners
are rounded but then the others connecting to it aren't? Fix that"*; *"The
clips for the case don't make sense either, because they aren't clipping to
anything"*; *"The badge case that's opened in the badge tab. Ensure the case
is better here too."*

> **Supersedes** build 317 badge2's "the case's name is on its side"
> (`buildCaseSidePlate` on the cutscene's and the Badges tab's front walls)
> and build 320's clips on the lid's top. The Profile card's small shut case
> (`.pf-ccase`) is not the kit's case and keeps its side plate.

**THE BACK'S WORDS ARE PLANNED AGAINST THE BACK'S OWN FIELD
(`badgeBackPlan`).** `badgeBackLayout` sized the name to the shape's
BOUNDING BOX (`b.w * S * .86`) and centred it there, so on every shape that
is not a box the words ran under the rim: the star, the bolt, the wedge, the
fan, the trefoil and the peaks lost letters, and on the C-ring nearly the
whole name was off the metal. Now, once per unit (cached, warmed with the
strikes 5s after launch, a few ms):
- `badgeBackField(g, W)` is the outline's signed distance as the back sees
  it (mirrored), at `planW` (260) px; a pixel is usable when it is
  `rimIn + margin` (4.6 + 1.6) units inside the outline;
- a column prefix-sum of unusable pixels makes "is this band of rows clear
  between x0 and x1" one lookup, and the runs per band are cached;
- every break of the words into 1-4 rows is tried at a size found by
  HALVING (`fsMin`..`fsMax`, ~12 sizes, not a 40-step descent - that took
  up to 1.2s for Code of Criminal Procedure); fewer rows win, then slack;
- every row sits on ONE centre line, the one nearest the shape's middle
  that all rows allow (per-row centring scattered the lines on the bolt and
  the peaks); the block is placed nearest the middle first and the first
  offset that fits is taken;
- "CLASS 26E" and its rule come along only if the name keeps `classKeep`
  (.96) of the size it has without them AND is at least `classNameMin`
  (5.6 units) anyway - on the wedge, the bolt, the peaks, the trefoil and
  the cross the name gets the room;
  (superseded in 326: every back carries CLASS 26E, `badgeBackPlan` -
  b326b.)
- **tidy breaks**: no row that is only AND / OF / THE, and round the ring no
  top line ending on one (a break after the comma preferred) - taken unless
  they cost more than `tidyKeep` (.9) of the size. Both searches run twice
  (strict, then loose). "MULTICULTURALISM / AND / HUMAN RELATIONS" and
  "CIVIL PROCESS / AND / LIABILITY" were the measured-best breaks and read
  as mistakes;
- **A RING HAS NO WIDE BAND ANYWHERE**, so `BADGE_SHAPE.cring.backArc`
  (`c`, inner and outer `r`, a smaller `margin` - the words run parallel to
  both edges) puts its words round it like a seal: the first part clockwise
  up the left and over the top (letters standing out), the rest along the
  bottom reading left to right (letters standing in), the turn at the lower
  left (`ARC_TURN`), a break after a comma preferred and one leaving AND/OF
  on the top line avoided. The ring is not quite round about any one point,
  so the words follow the band's own middle (measured per half degree,
  smoothed), and every glyph's box is tested against the field.
- The back's rim is narrower (`rimIn` 4.6 against the front's 6.4): the back
  only has to meet the front at the OUTLINE, where the edge turns; the inner
  profile is the front's pressed into the narrower band (`RIMK`).

**THE CUT READS (`BADGE_BACK_RELIEF`: `ink`, `inkK`, `fieldFlat`,
`fieldLevel`, `fieldDirt`).** The letters were the field's own grey with a
dark outline. Measured as a contrast ratio (median metal round the words :
median floor of the letters) the old backs were 0.95-2.6 clean. Three
changes, each found by measuring:
- the floor is blackened (an engraver's fill) from the words' UNSOFTENED
  coverage, so the fill runs to each letter's edge and the softened walls
  stay lit round it - from the softened mask, thin strokes never got dark;
  (superseded in 326: the words are a cut with lit walls and a darkened
  floor, not a fill edge to edge - b326b.)
- **brushed is satin, not mirror**: the field took the studio's reflection
  like the polished rim, so the same back was bright under the softbox and
  dark a few units away (fields measured .10 to .49 linear) and the peaks',
  the trefoil's and the fan's words sat on the dark side. Most of the
  field's light is now an even level, eased in from the rim's foot;
- the fill goes on AFTER the dirt, and the field dulls by `fieldDirt` (.55)
  of what the rim does - still visibly dirtier, still readable;
- **the satin is the FIELD's, never the cut's walls** (`* (1 - mk * 5)`):
  flattened too, the walls lost the studio's light and the letters lost
  their bright lower lip - check_b321d's "walls catch the light" fell from
  ~100 to 76-82 (needs 88). Exempt, it is 116-125.
Now 3.9-5.9 clean and 2.8+ at the dirtiest on every badge.

**ONE NAMEPLATE, ON TOP (`caseKit().nameplate`, `.nova-case-nameplate`).**
"NOVA · CLASS 26E", a rule, and the case's name (`badgeCaseName`) on one
plate on the lid's outside: its shadow on the leather (a gradient), its
thickness along the near edge (`.nova-case-np-edge`), a brushed slab with a
bevel and a fine chamfer line, the words stamped in (dark with a lit lower
lip), a rivet in each corner. Sizes in `--cu`, so it is the same plate in
the cutscene and on the Badges tab. It takes the lid's perspective because
it is ON the lid. The front walls carry no words; the handle hangs in the
middle of the wall (cutscene `top:40%`, tab `2.4cqw`). The case's name is
also still in the lid's cushion, where you read it once it is open.
`.nova-case-plate` stays on the nameplate (some older audits exclude it by
that class); its old flat style is overridden at `.nova-case
.nova-case-plate.nova-case-nameplate`.

**KEEPERS, NOT CLIPS (`caseKit().keeper`, `.nova-case-keeper`, still
`.nova-case-clip`).** The clips were on the lid's TOP while the hasps reached
up the FRONT and ended on bare leather. A keeper is a plate on the lid's
front over each latch with a staple (`.nova-case-staple`) standing out of it.
- **Cutscene**: shut, each hasp's slot is over its staple and the staple
  stands through it, in front (`.bc-lid-front` and the keeper are
  preserve-3d; the staple is `translateZ(3.5px)` over a hasp at 1.5px).
  **3D children of a 3D wall face their own way**: `.bc-lid-front` is
  backface-hidden, but its keepers (preserve-3d children) were not, and once
  the lid stood open they showed through its back as dark blocks along the
  lid's top edge. `.bc-keeper, .bc-keeper *` are backface-hidden.
  (superseded in 326: nothing under `.bc-lid` is preserve-3d; keepers and
  staples are painted flat on `.bc-lid-front` - b326b.)
  Letting go is two moves (`bc-hasp-free`): pulled out off the staple to
  -24deg on a springy curve, then down to -158deg. Both are done before
  `BC_T.crack` (left by ~8.32s, right by ~8.62s). The end pose is the
  class's own transform, so the still scene shows them down. **-42deg was
  tried first and the hasp vanished**: the camera looks down 52deg, so a
  hasp tipped 42deg towards you is seen edge-on.
- **Badges tab**: the shut lid's outside has the keepers at its near edge;
  `.is-latched` puts the hasps up over the seam and lifts the front over
  the lid (z 5). **The lid is its own layer**, so its staple cannot be put in
  front of a hasp that belongs to the base: `.ncase-staple-over` draws the
  staple again inside each latch, above its hasp, while hooked and through
  the lift (the slot is still over it), and goes as the hasp swings away -
  gone at the lift's start, the slot showed empty for ~100ms. `openBadgeCaseLid` now has
  `CASE_OPEN.unlatch` (380ms) after the hold: each hasp is lifted
  (`HASP_POP`) and swung down (`HASP_DOWN`), the right a beat after the left
  (`HASP_STAGGER`), and only then does the lid crack. ~1.48s in all (was
  1.1). The sound is scored from the first latch (`latch2`, `crack`,
  `swing` passed to `badge.case.open`).
- A keeper on the tab is as wide as a latch: `13%` of the front's CONTENT
  box (it has 15% padding each side), so 9.1% of the case. At 13% of the
  case the staples sat beside the hasps' slots.

**ONE CORNER (`--cap-w`, `--cap-ri`).** The caps on a top were flat plates
lit from the top left with a big curve on their free corner; the guards
under them were polished barrels lit across, a different width, with a
smaller curve at their foot, and the lid's front was rounded at the seam
over a base that was square there. Now a guard is the cap's plate (metal,
bevel, seat), exactly the cap's width from the case's outer edge (a cap
starts 2px out, over the shell's 2px trim; the guard starts at the wall's
edge - same edge), SQUARE wherever it meets another part (the fold under a
cap, the seam), and rounded only at its free foot, with the cap's own inner
curve. The right guard is the left mirrored (`scaleX(-1)`), so its light is
put back to the top left by hand. On the tab **the shut lid's outside sat
2px inside the case** (the lid is a trimmed shell: its own border) and the
lid's inside caps (z 3) showed through it as a second cap on every near
corner; `.ncase-lid-out` is inset -2px and at z 4 now.

**Gate: `tools/check-b325-b.py`** (both reference devices, installed;
`B325B_ONLY=A..F` for one section). Against 6fc16b7 every check fails (33

### Build 325 (b325c) - the wall is the next rank's level, a pool that empties, the tab that calls, a crack not a burn

Madison's list for stream C, in his words, and what each became. Branch
`b325c`. Gate: `tools/check-b325-c.py` (fails on 6fc16b7, passes here).

- **THE LEVEL WALL IS THE NEXT RANK'S LEVEL (supersedes build 314's
  bands).** *"The max level you can reach should the level your rank
  needs. So for platinum it says reach level 50, that should be your max
  level ... if you are unranked, the highest level you can reach is the
  level required for that first rank."* The cap is
  `TIER_UNLOCKS[next rank you do not hold].level`: unranked 21, Bronze
  30, Silver 40, Gold 50, Platinum 60, Sapphire 70, Amethyst and up 80.
  `wallRankIndex(badges, rankFloor)` finds that rank - the first one,
  from the one past any `rankFloor`, whose BADGES you lack (a rank whose
  badges you have asks for a level under the cap, so at the cap you hold
  it; that is also why the cap can never cost a rank). `badgeWallLevel`,
  `gateRankForBadges`, `levelWallOf` and `levelStateOf` all take the rank
  floor now (`levelStateFor` passes `st.rankFloor`; the results block and
  the rank-up numbers pass `store.rankFloor`). `rankOfStats` still clamps a
  published row with the badge-only wall, which cannot change an answer.
  - **NOBODY'S SHOWN LEVEL DROPS - a one-shot grandfather floor.** The
    wall moved down a whole block, so `levelWallMigrate325` runs once per
    account in `applyLoadedData()` for any copy without
    `levelWallRule >= 325`: the level build 324 showed
    (`min(curve, max(badgeWallLevel324(b), levelFloor))`) is kept as
    `levelFloor` wherever it is above the new cap. `levelWallRule` is on
    `store` (new account 325 in the store literal, a reset sets 325 and
    clears the floor), merged by max in `mergeSameAccount` and
    `mergeLeavingAccount`, as `levelFloor` already was - so two devices
    that each ran it agree on the higher of two levels that were each
    really shown, and nothing can ping-pong.
  - **IT MUST STAY ONE-SHOT.** Run again, it would read a higher old-rule
    level off XP earned since and lift the floor - the old rule leaking
    back. The residual window: a phone still on 324 strips the unknown
    field when it saves, and a 325 device loading that copy runs the
    migration again from that copy's XP. That can only ever RAISE a
    floor, to a level 324 itself was showing, so it is a leak of the old
    rule for someone still running 324, never a loss.
  - **Proved on real data, read-only:** the 40 rows of the live board on
    Oct 18 (XP, badges, published level - fetched with the public
    rankings list, ids dropped on read, nothing written) and the 44 Sep 30
    progress documents, each loaded by BOTH builds' own `applyLoadedData`
    / `levelStateFor` / `rankOf`: no level drops, no rank drops, no
    rises, the rankings row equals the shown level, a reload changes
    nothing; 7 accounts in each set are kept by the floor. Every board
    row loads at exactly the level it published.
    Note: most of the class's published levels are ABOVE build 324's own
    wall (Billyswole 40 with 0 badges against a 29 cap) - they carry
    `levelFloor`s from build 314's first, grandfathering version. Do not
    assume `levelFloor` is rare.
  - **Copy says the new rule.** What's New's level note
    (`levelGateNoteText`, "Levels wait for your next rank") no longer says
    "your level went from X to Y" - nobody's did; the Rank tab's map note,
    Nova's Profile tooltip and the two study tips say the level goes as
    high as the next rank's level and its badges take it further.
  - `tools/firestore-admin.py`'s `badge_wall`/`effective_level` follow the
    app (including the migration for a copy without the flag); check-curve
    9 compares them with the page.
- **Gates moved to the new rule, deliberately:** check-curve section 8
  (caps 21/30/30/40..., the jump at the badge to the curve, Profile at the
  wall "Level 21", the four-badge wall at 40, the row at 30; its fixtures
  carry `levelWallRule: 325` where they test the rule, not the
  migration); check_b319_rankup and check_b320d_rankup (the fixture is
  Silver at Gold's level 40, the journey climbs 40 -> 50 - Platinum's
  level, the next wall - not 49 -> 53). **Fixtures that load
  USED_ACCOUNT without the flag are grandfathered** (14,820 XP, 0 badges
  keeps level 25 as a floor): set `levelFloor = 0` (most already do) or
  `levelWallRule: 325` when a check needs the bare rule.
- **THE PROFILE TAB CALLS (supersedes build 320's "nothing on the tab
  moves").** *"it didn't seem like the profile tab on bottom was moving or
  shaking. The word profile was only highlighted yellow."* While Home is
  locked for a rank-up, `#bottomtab-profile` plays `.ru-nudge` - the
  "something new is in there" gesture (avatar-pulse's grow and ring, in
  the rank's colour, plus a short shake), ONCE per call: as the lock
  engages (`RU_NUDGE_FIRST_MS`), every `RU_NUDGE_EVERY_MS` (5s) while it
  stays locked and nothing holds Home (`rankUpLockWaits`), and on a
  refused tap (`rankUpNudge`, `rankUpNudgeArm`). 320's complaint was a
  ring breathing and the character bobbing on a loop; there is still no
  ring (::before) and nothing loops. Ring at 7px, scale 1.15 - at 14px
  and 1.18 the ring was clipped by the bar's top edge on a phone.
- **PROFILE'S XP BAR NO LONGER FILLS ON OPENING.** *"when you open
  profile the xp bar shouldn't move to right like how it does."*
  `buildProfileStanding` sets the fill at its value when it builds it (a
  new element takes its first `--fill` with no transition);
  `runXpBarFill` no longer moves it. The "earned since" knock into a full
  bar (317) stays and starts a beat after the tab is up (600ms). **A
  transform transition can finish on the compositor while the page is
  still building**, so sampling the bar after `showProfile()` returned
  saw it already full on 324 - the gate reads the value synchronously
  after the build and lists any transition on the fill.
- **THE SAVED XP IS A POOL THAT EMPTIES.** *"it should almost be
  subtracting, so you can see in realtime all the xp going to work."*
  During `rankUpStandingClimb` the right of the line under the bar (the
  total, or "to Level N") gives its place to `.ru-pool` - "SAVED XP" and
  the number, held full for `RU_POOL_LEAD_MS`, then counting DOWN in the
  same frame as the bar: what is left is `total - (xpForLevel(level) +
  min(shown into level, span))`, so it lands on `to.banked` when the
  climb stops at the next wall and 0 when not. Each level the bar
  completes lifts a "-N XP" off it (`rankUpPoolTake`, one per level even
  when two land in one frame). It holds `RU_POOL_HOLD_MS` and goes.
  **Driven a frame at a time (`ruTween`), not CSS keyframes**: a CSS
  animation started on that busy screen sat pending ~400ms in Chromium,
  so the pool came up late and every chip had gone before it moved.
  (superseded in 326: no pool; the extra is spent where it stands, on the
  number under the bar - b326c.)
- **A CLIMB THAT ENDS AT A WALL ENDED WITH THE BAR EMPTY - fixed.**
  `place(u1)` floored u1 to the level after the wall and drew it at 0%.
  The last level now holds the end of the climb. 324 never hit it in a
  gate (its fixture climbed to a level inside the wall); under the new
  rule a rank-up very often ends at the next rank's level.
- **THE RESULTS XP CARD ADDS UP ON ITS FACE.** *"the names of the xp and
  stuff and showing how it's calculated is hard to understand."*
  `computeRunXp` labels are plain and each line's sub-line is its sum:
  "Correct answers - 47 right × 10 XP", "Perfect units - 3 hundos × 100
  XP", "Answers in a row - 10 in a row +25 · 25 in a row +50", "Speed -
  9.0s a question on average (7:03 in all)", "Long test", "Best time /
  Best score / Personal bests", "Several units ×1.2 - +20% of the 955
  above, for 3 whole units". The card puts a "Bonuses" heading
  (`.rs-xpkick`) after the answers' line and "470 for answers + 675 in
  bonuses = 1,145 XP" (`.rs-xpsum`) under the total. Keys unchanged (the
  Virtual Room's steps match by key). check-results 5 asserted the
  literal "Streak bonus" - it now asserts the line is about answers in a
  row.
  (superseded in 326: `.rs-xpsum` is gone, the streak line is words
  ("Reached 10 twice and 25"), and "Perfect units" is "Hundo" - b326a.)
- **THE BLACK RINGS ARE RETIRED.** Decision: *"Maybe we just get rid of
  the black ones and only keep the new ones you get from reaching
  supernova?"* `homeRingTier()` is "supernova" or "". The full set of
  secret flares added only the rings; it keeps everything each flare
  gives. A device whose `ringtier.seen` is "eclipse" settles on orange
  with no draw. The planet's tap caption still says "the secret ones
  too" when every one is found. Eclipse drawing code is unreachable and
  kept for the record; release-notes history untouched.
- **THE RING STREAK AT RANDOM TIMES.** `homeStreakRandArm` runs it on its
  own clock, 12-38s apart (why "random"), beside the every-4th-pulse one
  and the tap one; same holds.
- **Gates moved for the rest:** check_b319_levelnote (the new note text,
  "nobody under the cap" at level 18), check_b317_rings (no top tier; the
  ring draw is held on plain -> orange; the black / "flares" / "white"
  style checks are gone with the tier), check_b321f_profile (Gold's wall
  50), check_b321h (a random streak may land between the pulses),
  check_b320e_cracks (no smoke; Supernova's lit crack walls count as drawn
  at alpha > 8 - a wider crack's wall facing the light is a pale sheen
  where Amethyst's narrower one was in shadow, 2.2% of its pixels),
  check_b317_xpcap and check_b320a_results F (their "room" and "fills to
  the wall this run" fixtures sat inside 324's walls), check-results 2
  (the streak line's sub now reads "10 in a row ×2 +50 · 25 in a row +50").
- What's New's "Supernova's mark" row says the crack and its glow, not
  smoke (`WHATS_NEW_320`; the version-history copy is left as history).
- **SUPERNOVA'S MARK IS A CRACK, NOT A BURN.** *"make it less burn mark and
  more crack like."* `SCAR_CRACK_ONLY`: the full stage draws the rank
  cracks' network at full width and depth - no crater (CR off), no soot
  round the impact, no scorch along the crack (`NOSCORCH`), the arms
  joined through the impact by the stretch the ranks below already have,
  a short star of fissures out of the impact (its own seed, `rnd3`), the
  shine broken into plates with nothing laid on them
  (`scarShineWound(..., clean)`) - and a faint light down the middle of
  every fissure (`P.GLOW`, the ember canvas), strongest on the arms. No
  smoke off it. Amethyst lost its scorch too, so every stage holds the
  one before. The ember's breathing floor is .7 (was .45: at its low the
  light read as brown char). A glow filling the crack's width read as a
  tan worm; it is the inner 40% now.
  (superseded in 326: the look - a larger crack with his light in it and
  motes drawn onto the rings; the rules stand - b326c.)
- **THE SECRET FLARES ORBIT IN THE CUTSCENE.** They did turn, on Home's
  clock (120s / 52s a lap) - beside the scene's bubbles (30s) that reads
  as standing still. In `.tier-cutscene` their rings run at 30s / 13s;
  the whirl (on `rotate`) adds on top. Measured ~11 degrees a second
  before and after the whirl, against ~3.
- **THE HAND-OFF: THE COPY WAS THE WRONG SIZE ON AN iPAD - the real
  "changes in the transition".** `rankUpHandOut` draws the copy back with a
  WAAPI `scale(.84)`, `fill: forwards`; `rankCutHandoff` cancelled it via
  `ghost.getAnimations()` and set the copy's own `scale(bubble/width)`
  inline. A FINISHED animation is not always in `getAnimations()`, but its
  fill still beats the inline transform - so the copy stayed at .84 of its
  220px stop box: 185px in the planet system, 59px off a 72px bubble whose
  rim then cut a gold stripe out of it. On the iPhone .84 happens to be the
  bubble's ratio (52/62), which is why it looked right there and why
  check_b320d's 2px check passed. The animation is now kept on the element
  (`ghost.__ruDraw`) and cancelled by name. **Never trust getAnimations()
  to find a finished fill-forwards animation you made: keep the handle.**
- **THE HAND-OFF LANDS IN A LIT BUBBLE.** *"the flare bubble changes in
  the transition and doesn't look like the flare."* The road map has lit
  the flare; the scene's planet-you-had kept that bubble DARK (grey glass)
  until the bang, so the gold copy faded into a grey ball. Opened with a
  hand-off, `rankCutHandoff` lights the bubble (`cosmic-badge-lit`, the
  flare's own `--tier-glow`, noir where it applies) on its first frame, so
  the copy fades into the same lit flare. Frame-stepped by freezing every
  timer and animation at `ru-handoff-in` and seeking them together.

### Build 325 (b325d) - Nova's story told in order, a signal for everyone who was here first, every unearned character blacked out, a Qualifier seal, his broadcast once per account

Madison: *"Nova walk through for new accounts, when it shows the characters
... only 4 even though it says 5 and it says there's 30 but only shows like
10 ... I really like how the characters are blacked out. Can we make it so
all the unlockable characters you don't have THAT aren't unlocked by a rank
do this? ... the challenge ones can all have the same challenge look, the
secret flare ones can be how they are, and the ultimate ones can be a little
cooler like a glow ... the badges are the same, mentions 16 badges and only
shows a few ... we can't say there were only 16 badges because they will be
more ... add another box or slide mentioning the challenges and stuff to
find them. The badge description is bad here, it's way too specific. This
walk through needs to feel like a story line ... the story line for the non
lit up flares doesn't make sense ... the explosion happening doesn't make
sense enough ... For existing accounts ... it needs to feel more surprising
... It doesn't mention virtual room ... Qualifier is a cool name, not a fan
of the icon though. Remove the skip button during this ... Remove all of
those from the what's new stuff ... only the ones with the 'new' at the
beginning need to be there, it doesn't need to say new though ... 'something
new, you can message me now' but I've seen it multiple times."*

- **The introduction is one story with causes, `novaIntroLines()`.** His
  ship was studying a planet like the one on Home that *had started to
  crack* (the crack Home's own planet grows from Gold up); its core gave way
  and it exploded; the blast threw everything aboard across the system. His
  flares, one per rank, came to rest around *your* planet with their light
  put out - that is why Home's flares are dark - and a flare only lights for
  someone who has earned it, which is what a rank is. A few secret flares
  were thrown further, into tests. His badges landed one in every unit. His
  crew got away in pods and are the characters. Then how each kind is found,
  XP/levels/rank, Drill/Qualifier/Briefing, **the Virtual Room (and
  challenging him there)**, the friend line (unchanged, `friend: true`), and
  the job: *light my flares, find my badges, bring my crew home*. 15 lines
  for a new account, 18 for an existing one. The wreck scene (`buildNovaWreck`)
  is untouched; the words around it now explain it. His goodbye, the Version 9
  "Nova, Your Instructor" note and his chat reply about flares/ship tell the
  same story.
  (superseded in 326: Briefing is Review again, the secret flares are
  "I've lost count of them", and the line counts changed - b326d,
  b326e, and the open questions at the end of the 326 block.)
- **An existing account is FOUND by him (`novaTalk` `signal`).** The overlay
  opens on his sky with nobody in it: a beacon pulses under "Incoming signal"
  for ~1.8s, collapses towards where he stands, and he arrives in it (2.4s;
  taps do nothing until he is there; Reduce motion skips it). "There you
  are, Madison ... I don't think we've met" (he liked that line), then "I've
  been following your progress, and you've already found some of what I
  lost" over the characters THEY own (`novaFoundRow`). The recap of what they
  have stays at the end (`recap: true`, `skipTo` for tools).
- **No number the stage does not show.** Characters: `novaCrewParade()` draws
  EVERY character (`novaCrewShown()` = Customize's own list) on a three-row
  slow pan (`novaParade`: each row glides to its far end and back, alternate
  rows the other way, the distance measured after layout; a row that fits
  does not move) under "N of M characters found" - both counted from the
  same list. Badges: `novaBadgeParade()` - every unit's badge, two rows, found
  ones in enamel, the rest as the grey form (lifted with a CSS filter so it
  reads on his sky; never its colour, build 319). **No badge total anywhere
  he speaks**: not in the line ("one into every unit you study. Master a unit
  and you'll find its badge."), not the caption ("Every unit has its own
  badge" / "3 badges found so far"), not `novaMeCard` (now "N badges found",
  not "N of 16"), not his chat reply.
- **"How they're found" is its own slide (`novaCrewKinds`).** One row per
  kind - Starters, Rank rewards, Challenges, Secrets, Ultimate - each with a
  character of that kind drawn in its locked look, one line on how, and
  "have of total", all counted from `AVATAR_CHARACTERS` via `charCategory()`.
  A character added to the table changes the numbers by itself.
- **Every unearned challenge, secret and ultimate character is blacked out
  (`charCategory`, `charLockLook`, `charSilhouetteSVG`).** One function
  decides the look by the table's own fields: `secret` keeps the 313/314
  cut-out exactly; `challenge` is one shared look - black hatched with the
  challenge strip's diagonal stripes (an SVG `<pattern>`, id from the
  drawing's own `data-cx-uid` so the flip-book hash is stable), edged in
  steel blue `#7FA3D6`; `ultimate` is black, edged in white gold with two
  wider, fainter copies of the edge under it (a drawn glow - no filter - so
  the recorded flip-book carries it) and a breathing gold pool behind the
  tile. **Rank characters keep the greyed preview**, as asked. The newer
  looks leave out each drawing's own light and weather (`SIL_LIGHT_RE`:
  lightning, code rain, glints, sparks, the lit backdrop) and edge filled
  shapes only (thin stroked details edged too showed as lines inside the
  black). Drawn in: Customize (`buildCustomizeCharacterSect`), the unlock
  card (`showUnlockDetail` art), the Detective's progress banner and the next
  secret's card (`buildCharArtFor`), and Nova's slides. Sign-up shows no
  locked characters, so nothing changes there.
  The ultimates also leave out their rings, orbits and halos (as black they
  were a disc that hid the figure), and the tallest cut-outs - Zeus, the
  Ronin and the three ultimates - are scaled onto their own shoulders
  (`SIL_FIG_FIT`, whole figure about (20, 37)) because the edge sits
  outside the drawing and reached the tile's top fade; check-b325-d holds
  every challenge and ultimate cut-out clear of the top 6%.
  **The secrets and ultimates move; the twelve challenge cut-outs hold
  still** - every moving tile is a flip-book recorded on the first visit,
  and twelve more of them made Void wait 179s for its own on a loaded
  machine (47s on base, 62s now). A locked challenge character never moved
  before either.
  **Trap:** a detached SVG's nodes all report `isConnected === false`, so a
  removal loop guarded on `n.isConnected` silently removed nothing - guard on
  `n.parentNode`.
- **No Skip (`novaTalk` `noSkip`)** on his introduction (both flows), the
  meeting's chained What's New and his goodbye; Escape does not skip there
  either. `el.__nova.skip` stays for tools that fast-forward. Decided on his
  behalf: the STANDALONE What's New (a device whose account already met him)
  and the weekly recap keep their Skip.
- **What's New (`WHATS_NEW_320`)**: "Results, grade first", "Characters
  celebrate", "Ranking up, on the road map", "A planet that cracks",
  "Supernova's mark" and "The daily question ring" are gone from his
  narration and still in the version history (Version 8). In: Qualifier and
  Briefing, Your study hours, Message Nova, Challenge Nova, The weekly recap.
  Kept: Sound effects, Calendar in the tab bar, Save a test for later, The
  Level 1 Badge Case. Nine rows.
  (superseded in 326: the recap and the badge case are off it and the row
  is "The Qualifier"; seven rows - b326d.)
- **The returning tips (`startNovaReturnTour`) are the three that said
  "New:" and nothing else**, without the word. New accounts still get the
  seven main-menu tips (`mainMenuTourSteps(false)`), unchanged.
- **"Something new: you can message me now" once per account.** Why it
  repeated: what he had said was recorded on the DEVICE only
  (`class26e.nova`), so every new device, every Safari jar beside the
  installed app and every fresh recording was owed it again; and his hello,
  sent ninety seconds before, already said "You can message me too". Now:
  `store.novaHeard` (id -> when; default `{}` in `applyLoadedData`, `maxMap`
  in `mergeSameAccount`, cleared by `wipeLocalProgressAndSettings`) records a
  delivered broadcast on the ACCOUNT; a device that delivered one before this
  build writes it in on its next tick; and a broadcast marked `hello: true`
  (v9-dms) is never owed to a friendship that began after its `at`. The
  record is written with `persistLocally()` and rides along with the next
  real save - nothing of his pushes the progress document by itself (b324n
  still holds that).
- **The Qualifier's mark is a rosette seal** (`modeIcon("exam")`): a scalloped
  seal at the target's stroke weight, two solid ribbon tails (`modeiconsolid`,
  like the Virtual Room's solid heads) and the bold tick. Not the shield.
  Every Qualifier icon comes from `modeIcon`; the Version 9 note's row and
  Nova's What's New row now use it too (a filled-glyph copy for `introRow`).
  (superseded in 326: the mark is a tick going out through a ring -
  b326d.)
- **Parades are drawn ahead** (`novaWarmProps`): thirty characters and every
  badge were ~1s of drawing at the moment he moved on to the line - a stall
  in his typing; they are made ~12ms at a time while he says hello and the
  planet goes, and taken from a cache. Under Reduce motion nothing pans, so
  the parade is one wrapped grid (three rows of ten on a phone).
- **Gates moved to this decision**: check-behaviour b320f/b321g (no Skip -
  tools fast-forward with `el.__nova.skip()`; "3 badges found"; the new tips
  alone; the story's new words; the harness waits out the signal), b314_chars
  and b317_silhouettes (their "no colour" and "four tiles" rules are the
  SECRETS', so they measure `.is-sil-secret`), check-chat's introduction
  section (fast-forward; Version 9's rows), check-tours (`novareturn` counts
  the main menu's tips only if the function still asks for them),
  check-unlocks' locked-art section (the greyed treatment is a rank
  character's now; the Masked One's tile is given back its real drawing to
  measure the filter on).
- **Gate `tools/check-b325-d.py`** (46 checks; all fail on 6fc16b7): the
  story's order and causes, the Virtual Room, no badge total and every unit's
  badge drawn, every character drawn with honest counts, the kinds box from
  the table, no Skip/Escape, the signal (and none under Reduce motion), the
  meeting's order and its tips, What's New's six out / six additions in /
  history kept, the broadcast across two devices and a new account, the
  merge/default, the three locked looks in Customize and on the card, the
